# File system

The commands `mt help` lists under File system. These work on the files of a file system the way a terminal's commands work on a disk's. More in [File systems](../../../concepts/file-systems.md).

In a terminal, type `mt` and then the command. In the interactive shell and the cloud shell, type the command on
its own. `mt help <command>` shows the same details in your terminal.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`batch-edit`](#batch-edit) | Edit several files of a file system at once, from a JSON file of edits (all or nothing unless `--not-atomic`) |
| [`batch-read`](#batch-read) | Print several files of a file system at once (exits 1 if any cannot be read) |
| [`cat`](#cat) | Print a file's text, from your disk or a file system |
| [`cd`](#cd) | Change the working directory, which relative paths start from |
| [`cp`](#cp) | Copy a file or directory, also between your disk and a file system (overwrites existing files) |
| [`edit`](#edit) | Edit a file in a file system: find and replace text, replace or delete lines, or insert after a line |
| [`exists`](#exists) | Check whether a file or directory exists in a file system (exits 1 if it does not) |
| [`find`](#find) | Find files in a file system by a glob pattern on their path, by their text, or both |
| [`ls`](#ls) | List the files and directories in a directory (ls /vfs lists your file systems) |
| [`mkdir`](#mkdir) | Create a directory, and any parent directories it needs |
| [`mv`](#mv) | Move or rename a file or directory, also between your disk and a file system (copies it, then deletes the source) |
| [`rm`](#rm) | Delete a file, or a directory and everything in it (there is no confirmation) |
| [`tree`](#tree) | Show a directory of a file system, and everything below it, as a tree |
| [`write`](#write) | Write text to a file in a file system, replacing it or adding to its end (its directory must exist) |

## batch-edit

Edit several files of a file system at once, from a JSON file of edits (all or nothing unless `--not-atomic`).

```text
mt batch-edit <vfs> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<vfs>` | text | yes |  | The file system, as &lt;name>@&lt;namespace> (e.g. notes@default) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--edits-file, -f <value>` | text | yes |  | JSON file of edits (relative, /local/... or /vfs/...): an array of {"path", "operations": [{"type": "replace"\|"replaceLines"\|"insertAfter"\|"deleteLines", ...}]} |
| `--not-atomic` | flag |  |  | Keep the edits that succeed even if others fail (default: if any fails, no file changes) |

## batch-read

Print several files of a file system at once (exits 1 if any cannot be read).

```text
mt batch-read <vfs> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<vfs>` | text | yes |  | The file system, as &lt;name>@&lt;namespace> (e.g. notes@default) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--paths <value>` | text | yes |  | The files' paths in the file system, comma-separated (e.g. /README.md,/src/app.ts) |
| `--max-lines <number>` | whole number |  |  | Most lines to read from each file (0 for no limit) |

## cat

Print a file's text, from your disk or a file system.

```text
mt cat <path> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | File to read, relative or absolute |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--lines` | flag |  |  | Also return the text as a list of lines, for programs reading the command's result |
| `--number` | flag |  |  | Number each line |

## cd

Change the working directory, which relative paths start from.

```text
mt cd [path]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text |  |  | Directory to go to: relative, or absolute as /vfs/&lt;name>@&lt;namespace>/... or /local/... (mt only) |

## cp

Copy a file or directory, also between your disk and a file system (overwrites existing files).

```text
mt cp <source> <destination>
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<source>` | text | yes |  | File or directory to copy |
| `<destination>` | text | yes |  | Where to copy it: a new path, or an existing directory to copy it into |

## edit

Edit a file in a file system: find and replace text, replace or delete lines, or insert after a line.

```text
mt edit <path> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | File to edit, as /vfs/&lt;name>@&lt;namespace>/&lt;path> (relative paths are not accepted) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--find <value>` | text |  |  | Text to find, exactly and case-sensitively, and replace with `--replace` |
| `--replace <value>` | text |  |  | Text to put in place of `--find` (default: nothing, which deletes it) |
| `--replace-all` | flag |  |  | Replace every occurrence of `--find`, not just the first |
| `--start-line <number>` | whole number |  |  | First line to replace with `--content` (1-based; needs `--end-line`) |
| `--end-line <number>` | whole number |  |  | Last line to replace with `--content` (1-based, inclusive; needs `--start-line`) |
| `--content <value>` | text |  |  | The new text, for `--start-line` and `--end-line` or for `--insert-after` |
| `--insert-after <number>` | whole number |  | `-1` | Insert `--content` after this line (0 for the top of the file; -1 inserts nothing) |
| `--delete-lines <value>` | text |  |  | Line numbers to delete, comma-separated (e.g. 5,10,15) |

## exists

Check whether a file or directory exists in a file system (exits 1 if it does not).

```text
mt exists <path> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | Path to check, as /vfs/&lt;name>@&lt;namespace>/&lt;path> (relative paths are not accepted) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--directory` | flag |  |  | Check for a directory instead of a file |

## find

Find files in a file system by a glob pattern on their path, by their text, or both.

```text
mt find <path> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | Directory to search, as /vfs/&lt;name>@&lt;namespace>/&lt;path> (relative paths are not accepted) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--pattern <value>` | text |  |  | Glob the whole path from the file system's root must match, ignoring case (e.g. **/*.cs, /src/**/*.ts) |
| `--grep <value>` | text |  |  | Only files whose text contains this (plain text unless `--regex`) |
| `--regex` | flag |  |  | Treat `--grep` as a regular expression |
| `--ignore-case` | flag |  |  | Match `--grep` regardless of case |
| `--context <number>` | whole number |  |  | Lines to include before and after each `--grep` match |
| `--preview` | flag |  |  | Include the first lines of each file found |
| `--preview-lines <number>` | whole number |  | `30` | How many lines `--preview` includes |
| `--max-results <number>` | whole number |  | `100` | Most results to return |
| `--max-depth <number>` | whole number |  | `-1` | How many directories deep to search (-1 for no limit) |
| `--type <value>` | text |  | `file` | What to find: file, directory or all |
| `--hidden` | flag |  |  | Include hidden files and directories (names starting with .) |

## ls

List the files and directories in a directory (ls /vfs lists your file systems).

```text
mt ls [path]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text |  |  | Directory to list, relative or absolute (default: the working directory) |

## mkdir

Create a directory, and any parent directories it needs.

```text
mt mkdir <path>
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | Directory to create, relative or absolute |

## mv

Move or rename a file or directory, also between your disk and a file system (copies it, then deletes the source).

```text
mt mv <source> <destination>
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<source>` | text | yes |  | File or directory to move |
| `<destination>` | text | yes |  | Where to move it: a new path, or an existing directory to move it into |

## rm

Delete a file, or a directory and everything in it (there is no confirmation).

```text
mt rm <path>
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | File or directory to delete |

## tree

Show a directory of a file system, and everything below it, as a tree.

```text
mt tree <path> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | Directory to show, as /vfs/&lt;name>@&lt;namespace>/&lt;path> (relative paths are not accepted) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-depth <number>` | whole number |  | `-1` | How many levels deep to go (-1 for no limit) |
| `--files` | flag |  |  | Include files, not just directories (default: true; `--files` false for directories only) |
| `--hidden` | flag |  |  | Include hidden files and directories (names starting with .) |
| `--pattern <value>` | text |  |  | Only files whose whole path from the file system's root matches this glob (e.g. **/*.md) |
| `--flat` | flag |  |  | Print an indented list with file sizes instead of a tree |

## write

Write text to a file in a file system, replacing it or adding to its end (its directory must exist).

```text
mt write <path> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<path>` | text | yes |  | File to write, as /vfs/&lt;name>@&lt;namespace>/&lt;path> (relative paths are not accepted) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--content <value>` | text | yes |  | The text to write |
| `--lines` | flag |  |  | Send the text as lines, split at each newline (the file holds the same text either way) |
| `--append` | flag |  |  | Add the text to the end of the file instead of replacing it |
